title: SSC-1.2 — Explicit Aspect Checkpoint Evidence
summary: record the explicit registered aspect model, bounded future seams, access-safe projection and checkpoint verification
content_html:
SSC-1.2 — Explicit Aspect Checkpoint Evidence

Outcome

Each sub-scope customisation definition now declares typed optional aspects for manifest projection, document groups, source validation, metadata read/update, import front matter, and access-specific browser composition. Analysis Tags declares manifest, document-group, and Manage browser aspects. Projects declares manifest, validation, metadata, import, and Manage browser aspects. Their existing callback owners and current settings remain unchanged.

The definition also owns typed assignable_field_groups and transfer seams. A field group carries one registered group identity and its server-owned field names. A transfer declaration carries one contract identity and its server-owned field names. Both current registrations retain the empty field-group tuple and None transfer value; SSP/TDL and Copy remain the owning deliveries for concrete declarations and behavior.

Registry validation checks definition identity, aspect types and callbacks, supported browser accesses, manifest/browser coupling, unique group identities and field names, Manage access for assignable groups, and transfer identity. Access now derives from the browser-composition aspect instead of parallel public/Manage booleans.

Access-Safe Exact-Collection Projection

Manage browser configuration serializes the registered customisation identity and, when declared, only the assignable field-group IDs needed for availability. Validated settings, concrete field names, and transfer declarations remain in the server registry. Current Analysis Tags and Projects descriptors therefore remain exactly {id} and their public descriptor projection remains empty.

The browser normalizer accepts the identity plus the bounded capability envelope and exposes hasDocsViewerAssignableFieldGroup() for focused actions or modals. A builder fixture registers a synthetic assignable group on one exact configured collection and proves that only that collection receives the capability; the adjacent default collection retains its ordinary record, and the public projection retains ordinary public records. Availability derives from the configured collection's resolved definition rather than another flag or collection-name branch.

Verification

  • Focused registry, config, builder, source-model, metadata, import, watcher, package, public-boundary, migration, and seed tests: 179 passed, 1 skipped.
  • Docs Viewer sub-scope report browser-module smoke: passed, including basic and capability-bearing descriptor normalization, group availability, and strict capability validation.
  • Analysis Tags sub-scope build: 249 documents, zero document or manifest writes, zero warnings, and unchanged Manage/public browser configs.
  • Explicit Python lint: four affected Python files passed.
  • Explicit JavaScript lint: the affected shared config controller passed.
  • Source scan found one definition registry and current aspect members; current executable consumers use the new members and the generated Analysis Tags projection remains byte-current.
  • git diff --check: passed.

Review And Next Gate

The separate diff pass confirmed one bounded definition record, aspect-specific callback owners, one access set owned by browser composition, group-ID-only Manage capability projection, server-only transfer declarations, and exact configured-collection selection. The current manifests, rows, metadata, import normalization, browser factories, actions, and public isolation retain their established owners and values.

Action rendering, focused modals, subject/tag assignment, mutation services, concrete field groups, transfer behavior, durable architecture replacement, SSP-0 work, and TDL-0 work remain with their named later deliveries. SSC-1.3 owns final registration reconciliation, broader verification, durable architecture transfer, and consumer-document handoff. Stop for review before SSC-1.3.
